intro.title: Attribute selectors
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that styles different types of input fields based on their HTML attributes. You will learn how to use CSS attribute selectors to target elements by their attributes, such as type, placeholder, or required status. The main technology involved is CSS, specifically using selectors like [type="text"] and [required] to apply specific styles. By the end, you'll understand how to precisely style elements without adding extra classes, making your CSS more efficient and maintainable.
intro.usecase: Attribute selectors are essential for styling dynamic web interfaces where elements share data attributes but need distinct visual treatments. In e-commerce filters, they target checkboxes with specific data-filter attributes to highlight active selections. Dashboard developers use them to style status indicators based on data-status attributes like 'pending' or 'approved'. They also simplify form validation by styling inputs with aria-invalid attributes, and help theme systems apply styles to elements with data-theme attributes.
